attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.hse_incident. Business justification: Subrogation recovery actions against third parties often stem from HSE incidents (contractor negligence causing injury and cargo damage, equipment supplier fault). Legal teams require HSE incident evi

attributes.name: lane_id

attributes.name: settlement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to claim.claim_settlement. Business justification: Subrogation case is initiated after the insurer/carrier settles the claim with the claimant. 1:1 or N:1 relationship (one subrogation case per settlement). Adding claim_settlement_id FK allows normali

attributes.description: Reference to the insurer or underwriter who settled the original cargo claim and is now the subrogating party pursuing recovery from the liable third party.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to document.transport_document. Business justification: Demand letters are formal legal documents initiating subrogation recovery. attributes.description: Name of the arbitration institution or tribunal handling the subrogation dispute (e.g., ICC International Court of Arbitration, LMAA, AAA). Populated when case_status is arbitration.

attributes.name: case_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field capturing key case developments, negotiation positions, legal strategy notes, and correspondence summaries maintained by the assigned claims handler.

attributes.name: case_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference number assigned to the subrogation case, used in all correspondence with insurers, legal counsel, and third-party respondents. Format: SUB-YYYY-NNNNNN.

attributes.name: case_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the subrogation case. Tracks progression from initial opening through demand, negotiation, legal or arbitration proceedings, to final closure. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: open|demand_issued|negotiation|legal_proceedings|arbitration|settled|closed_recovered|closed_unrecovered|withdrawn — promote to reference product]

[ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: cargo_loss|cargo_damage|delay|dangerous_goods|misdelivery|theft|contamination — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CMR Convention; Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 18; IMDG Code; Hague-Visby Rules

attributes.name: closure_date
attributes.description: Date on which the subrogation case was formally closed, either following successful recovery, settlement, exhaustion of legal remedies, or commercial decision to withdraw.

attributes.name: closure_reason
attributes.description: Reason for closing the subrogation case. Captures the outcome basis for recovery P&L analysis and third-party liability management reporting. attributes.name: court_jurisdiction
attributes.description: Legal jurisdiction (country and court) in which legal proceedings have been or will be filed against the respondent party. Determined by applicable liability convention and contract terms.

attributes.name: created_timestamp

attributes.name: dangerous_goods_flag

attributes.name: dangerous_goods_un_number
attributes.description: United Nations dangerous goods identification number for the hazardous cargo involved in the loss event. Populated only when dangerous_goods_flag is true.
attributes.references: IMDG Code (IMO); ICAO Technical Instructions; IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations; UN Recommendations on Transport of Dangerous Goods

attributes.name: demand_letter_date
attributes.description: Date on which the formal demand letter was issued to the respondent party requesting recovery of the subrogation amount. Marks the formal commencement of the recovery action.
attributes.references: CMR Convention Article 32; Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 35; Marine Insurance Act 1906

attributes.name: external_legal_counsel

attributes.name: incoterms_code
attributes.description: International Commercial Terms (Incoterms) applicable to the underlying shipment, determining the point of risk transfer between buyer and seller and influencing liability attribution in the subrogation case. attributes.references: ICC Incoterms 2020; WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement; CMR Convention; Hague-Visby Rules

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the subrogation case record. Used for change tracking, audit compliance, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; GDPR Article 5; ISO 28000 Supply Chain Security Management

attributes.name: legal_costs_incurred
attributes.description: Cumulative legal and professional fees incurred in pursuing the subrogation recovery, including attorney fees, court filing fees, expert witness costs, and arbitration fees. Used in recovery P&L tracking.

attributes.name: legal_filing_date

attributes.name: liability_convention

attributes.name: liability_limit_amount
attributes.description: Maximum liability amount applicable to the respondent under the governing international convention (e.g., SDR per kg under CMR, SDR per kg under Hague-Visby). Constrains the maximum recoverable amount.

attributes.name: loss_event_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the country where the cargo loss or damage event occurred. Used for jurisdictional determination and applicable liability convention selection.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; CMR Convention; Warsaw-Montreal Convention; WCO Standards

attributes.name: loss_event_date
attributes.description: Date on which the cargo loss, damage, delay, or other qualifying event occurred that gave rise to the original claim and subsequent subrogation right.
attributes.references: CMR Convention Article 32; Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 35; Hague-Visby Rules Article III Rule 6

attributes.name: loss_event_location
attributes.description: Geographic location (port, terminal, warehouse, road segment, airport) where the cargo loss or damage event occurred. Determines jurisdiction and applicable liability convention.
attributes.references: CMR Convention; Hague-Visby Rules; Warsaw-Montreal Convention; IMO IMDG Code

attributes.name: opened_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the subrogation case was formally opened following settlement of the originating cargo claim. Marks the start of the recovery pursuit period.
attributes.references: CMR Convention Article 32; Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 35; Marine Insurance Act 1906

attributes.name: recovery_amount_received
attributes.description: Actual monetary amount recovered from the respondent party to date. Populated incrementally as payments are received and updated upon final case closure.
attributes.references: IFRS 4 Insurance Contracts; SAP S/4HANA Finance AR Module; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: recovery_amount_sought
attributes.description: Total monetary amount being demanded from the respondent party in the subrogation recovery action. May differ from the settlement amount due to contributory negligence, liability caps, or partial recovery strategy.
attributes.references: CMR Convention Article 23; Hague-Visby Rules Article IV bis; Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 22

attributes.name: recovery_currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which recovery amounts are denominated and tracked for this subrogation case.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; IFRS 21 Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates

attributes.name: recovery_rate_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of the recovery amount sought that was actually recovered from the respondent party. Calculated as (recovery_amount_received / recovery_amount_sought) * 100. Key KPI for subrogation P&L performance tracking.
attributes.references: IFRS 4 Insurance Contracts; SOX Section 404; SAP S/4HANA Finance P&L Reporting

attributes.name: cargo_survey_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to claim.cargo_survey. Business justification: Individual claim line items may reference specific survey findings that assessed damage to that particular commodity/SKU. N:1 relationship (many line items per survey). Adding cargo_survey_id FK allow

attributes.name: consignment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the shipment record against which this claim line is raised. Links the damaged or lost cargo line to the originating transport movement for liability and subrogation analysis.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; IMO Liability Conventions

attributes.name: customer_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.customer_account. Business justification: Claim lines track customer-specific cargo items and SKUs. Enables SKU-level claim analysis per customer, customer product risk profiling, and customer-specific packaging/handling recommendations. Crit

attributes.name: customs_declaration_line_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customs.declaration_line. Business justification: Line-level claims need line-level customs data to match specific commodities, verify per-item declared values (liability caps per package/unit), and validate HS codes. Essential for multi-commodity sh

attributes.name: freight_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to freight.freight_order. Business justification: Claim lines itemize damaged/lost cargo from specific freight orders. Essential for line-level damage assessment, SKU-level loss calculation, and linking claimed items to original shipment manifest for

attributes.name: lane_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.lane. Business justification: Individual claim lines (damaged SKUs) are analyzed by lane for loss-ratio reporting, carrier scorecarding, and commodity-specific risk assessment. Enables lane-level profitability analysis adjusted fo

attributes.name: order_line_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to fulfillment.order_line. Business justification: Claims are filed against specific order line items (SKU-level damage, quantity discrepancies, wrong item shipped). Finance and operations need line-item traceability for accurate settlement calculatio

attributes.name: approved_quantity
attributes.description: Quantity approved by the claims assessor following survey and investigation. May differ from claimed_quantity where partial loss or damage is confirmed. Used in settlement calculation.
attributes.references: IATA Cargo Claims Handling Manual; ISO 9001

attributes.name: approved_value
attributes.description: Monetary value approved for settlement on this line item following assessment, survey, and liability determination. May be less than claimed_value due to liability caps, depreciation, or partial loss findings.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; CMR Convention; IFRS 13

attributes.name: claim_filing_date
attributes.description: Date on which this claim line was formally filed with the carrier or insurer. Used to assess compliance with statutory filing deadlines under the Montreal Convention (14 days for damage, 21 days for delay) and CMR Convention.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 31; CMR Convention Article 30

attributes.name: claim_type
attributes.description: Classification of the nature of the claim line: loss (cargo not delivered), damage (cargo delivered in damaged condition), shortage (partial quantity missing), delay (late delivery causing financial loss), contamination, or pilferage. Drives liability framework selection.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; CMR Convention; IMO Liability Conventions

attributes.name: claimed_quantity
attributes.description: Number of units, pieces, or cargo items being claimed on this line. Represents the quantity declared as lost, damaged, or short-shipped by the claimant.
attributes.references: IATA Cargo Claims Handling Manual; WCO

attributes.name: claimed_value
attributes.description: Total monetary value claimed by the claimant for this line item, calculated as claimed_quantity multiplied by unit_value plus any ancillary costs. Represents the claimant's gross demand before assessment.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; CMR Convention; IFRS 13

attributes.name: commodity_description
attributes.description: Free-text description of the commodity or cargo item being claimed, as declared on the Air Waybill (AWB) or Bill of Lading (BOL). Used for customs reporting and insurer correspondence.
attributes.references: WCO Harmonized System Nomenclature; IATA AWB Standards

attributes.name: condition_at_destination
attributes.description: Recorded condition of the cargo item upon delivery at destination, as noted on the Proof of Delivery (POD) or cargo survey report. Compared against condition_at_origin to establish loss or damage.
attributes.references: IATA Cargo Claims Handling Manual; CMR Convention; ePOD Standards

attributes.name: condition_at_origin
attributes.description: Recorded condition of the cargo item at the point of origin or acceptance by the carrier, as noted on the AWB, BOL, or cargo receipt. Establishes the baseline for damage assessment and liability determination.
attributes.references: IATA Cargo Acceptance Standards; CMR Convention; WCO

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this claim line record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail, SLA measurement, and data lineage tracking in the Silver Layer lakehouse.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary values on this claim line (claimed_value, approved_value, unit_value). Ensures consistent multi-currency claim valuation and financial reporting.

attributes.name: damage_category
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the damage type for this claim line, enabling trend analysis and root cause reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: physical|water|fire|theft|contamination|temperature|handling|vermin|customs_examination — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IATA Cargo Claims Handling Manual; IMDG Code; ICAO Technical Instructions

attributes.name: damage_description
attributes.description: Detailed free-text description of the nature and extent of damage, loss, or shortage observed for this claim line item. Captured from cargo survey reports and used in insurer correspondence and settlement negotiations.
attributes.references: IATA Cargo Claims Handling Manual; ISO 9001

attributes.name: dangerous_goods_class
attributes.description: IMDG/ICAO dangerous goods classification class or division for the cargo item (e.g., Class 3 Flammable Liquids, Division 6.1 Toxic Substances). Populated only when is_dangerous_goods is true. Required for regulatory incident reporting.
attributes.references: IMDG Code; ICAO Technical Instructions for Dangerous Goods; IATA DGR

attributes.name: depreciation_rate
attributes.description: Depreciation rate applied to the cargo item's declared value to reflect age, wear, or market value reduction at the time of loss or damage. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.1500 = 15%). Applied in approved_value calculation.
attributes.references: IATA Cargo Claims Handling Manual; IFRS 13

attributes.name: destination_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the cargo destination for this claim line. Used for cross-border claims, import duty recovery, and jurisdictional liability framework determination.

attributes.name: gross_weight_kg
attributes.description: Gross weight in kilograms of the cargo items on this claim line as declared on the AWB or BOL. Used for liability cap calculation under weight-based conventions (e.g., Montreal Convention SDR per kg).
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 22; CMR Convention Article 23; IATA AWB Standards

attributes.name: hs_code
attributes.description: Harmonized System (HS) Code classifying the commodity under the World Customs Organization (WCO) nomenclature. Required for customs and trade compliance reporting, particularly for cross-border claims and duty recovery under DDP or DAP Incoterms.
attributes.references: WCO Harmonized System; Descartes Customs GTM

attributes.name: incoterms_code
attributes.description: International Commercial Terms (Incoterms) applicable to the shipment for this claim line, determining the point of risk transfer between buyer and seller. Influences liability determination and insurable interest. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EXW|FCA|CPT|CIP|DAP|DPU|DDP|FAS|FOB|CFR|CIF — 11 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: insurer_reference
attributes.description: Reference number assigned by the cargo insurer for this claim line. Used for insurer correspondence, subrogation tracking, and recovery management.
attributes.references: IATA Cargo Claims Handling Manual; ISO 28000

attributes.name: is_dangerous_goods
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the cargo item on this claim line is classified as dangerous goods under IMDG Code or ICAO Technical Instructions. Triggers specialist handling procedures and regulatory notification requirements for dangerous goods claims.
attributes.references: IMDG Code; ICAO Technical Instructions for Dangerous Goods; IATA DGR

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this claim line record. Supports change data capture (CDC) in the Databricks Silver Layer and audit compliance under SOX.

attributes.name: liability_basis
attributes.description: The legal or contractual framework governing carrier liability for this claim line. Determines the applicable liability cap and burden of proof. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: montreal_convention|cmr_convention|hague_visby|cotif|contractual|waiver — promote to reference product if additional conventions are added]
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; CMR Convention; Hague-Visby Rules; COTIF; IMO

attributes.name: liability_cap_value
attributes.description: Maximum carrier liability applicable to this claim line under the governing convention or contract (e.g., SDR per kg under Montreal Convention for air, or CMR limits for road). Constrains the approved_value ceiling.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 22; CMR Convention Article 23; IMO

attributes.name: line_number
attributes.description: Sequential line number ordering this item within the parent claim. Used for display, sorting, and referencing individual line items in insurer correspondence and settlement documentation.

attributes.name: line_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this individual claim line item. Tracks the workflow state from initial registration through assessment, approval or rejection, and final settlement or withdrawal.
attributes.references: IATA Cargo Claims Handling Manual; ISO 9001 Quality Management

attributes.name: loss_discovery_date
attributes.description: Date on which the loss, damage, or shortage for this claim line was first discovered or reported by the consignee or shipper. Critical for determining claim filing timeliness under applicable liability conventions.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 31; CMR Convention Article 30; Hague-Visby Rules

attributes.name: origin_country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the cargo origin for this claim line. Used for cross-border claims, customs duty recovery, and WCO trade compliance reporting.

attributes.name: quantity_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the claimed quantity (e.g., PCS for pieces, KG for kilograms, CBM for cubic metres, CTN for cartons, PLT for pallets, BAG for bags). Aligns with the unit declared on the AWB or BOL.

attributes.name: rejection_reason
attributes.description: Free-text or coded reason for rejection of this claim line, populated when line_status is 'rejected'. Documents the basis for denial (e.g., late filing, inherent vice, force majeure, insufficient evidence) for audit and dispute resolution.
attributes.references: IATA Cargo Claims Handling Manual; CMR Convention; ISO 9001

attributes.name: salvage_value
attributes.description: Residual monetary value of the damaged cargo recovered through salvage operations for this claim line. Deducted from the approved_value to determine the net settlement payable.
attributes.references: IATA Cargo Claims Handling Manual; IFRS 13 Fair Value

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: Date on which the claim line was financially settled and payment was made or credit note issued to the claimant. Used for finance reserve accounting and SAP S/4HANA AR reconciliation.
attributes.references: IFRS 9 Financial Instruments; SOX; SAP S/4HANA Finance

attributes.name: sku_code
attributes.description: Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) identifier for the specific product or cargo item being claimed. Sourced from the shipper's inventory or WMS system (Manhattan WMS) to enable granular claim valuation at the item level.
attributes.references: Manhattan WMS SKU Master; GS1 Standards

attributes.name: subrogation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether subrogation rights have been exercised or are being pursued for this claim line, enabling the insurer to recover costs from the liable carrier or third party after settlement.
attributes.references: IATA Cargo Claims Handling Manual; IMO Liability Conventions

attributes.name: subrogation_recovery_value
attributes.description: Monetary amount recovered through subrogation proceedings for this claim line. Populated after recovery is confirmed. Used in finance for net claims cost reporting and P&L impact analysis.
attributes.references: IFRS 9; SOX; IATA Cargo Claims Handling Manual

attributes.name: survey_date
attributes.description: Date on which the cargo survey or physical inspection was conducted for this claim line item. Used to track assessment timelines and SLA compliance for claims processing.
attributes.references: IATA Cargo Claims Handling Manual; ISO 9001

attributes.name: transport_mode
attributes.description: Mode of transport applicable to this claim line, determining the governing liability convention (IATA Warsaw-Montreal for air, Hague-Visby/CMR for ocean/road, COTIF for rail). Critical for liability cap calculation.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; CMR Convention; COTIF Convention; IMO

attributes.name: unit_value
attributes.description: Declared or assessed value per unit of the cargo item at origin, as stated on the commercial invoice. Used as the basis for claim valuation and liability cap comparison under applicable conventions.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; CMR Convention; IFRS 13 Fair Value

attributes.name: volume_cbm
attributes.description: Volume in cubic metres (CBM) of the cargo items on this claim line. Used for dimensional weight (DIM Weight) calculations and ocean freight LCL/FCL claim assessments.
attributes.references: IATA DIM Weight Standards; IMO; WCO

products.name: claim_party
products.description: Association entity linking all parties involved in a cargo claim to their respective roles and responsibilities. Captures party type (claimant, carrier, sub-carrier, insurer, underwriter, surveyor, legal counsel, customs authority, port operator, freight handler), party reference ID, contact details, notification status, response deadlines, and role-specific attributes. Enables multi-party claim management across complex intermodal and cross-border shipments where liability may be shared among multiple carriers and intermediaries.

attributes.name: claim_party_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each claim party association record in the Transport Shipping claims management system. Primary key for the claim_party entity.

attributes.name: cargo_claim_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent cargo claim record to which this party is associated. Links the party to the specific claim event.

attributes.name: contract_party_id
attributes.description: Reference to the master party record (organisation or individual) involved in this claim. Enables lookup of full party profile from the master party registry.
attributes.references: Salesforce CRM Account Object; GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: policy_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to claim.claim_policy. Business justification: Claim party involvement (especially insurer parties) is under a specific insurance policy. N:1 relationship (many party records per policy). Adding claim_policy_id FK allows normalization of policy_nu

attributes.name: aeo_number
attributes.description: AEO certification number of the party where applicable (carriers, freight handlers, customs brokers). Relevant for customs authority and freight handler roles in cross-border claims.
attributes.references: AEO Programme; WCO SAFE Framework; C-TPAT; Descartes Customs

attributes.name: awb_number
attributes.description: Air Waybill number associated with this party's involvement in the claim, applicable when the transport mode is air freight. Links to the specific air cargo consignment under IATA conventions.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 600; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; HAWB/MAWB standards

attributes.name: bol_number
attributes.description: Bill of Lading number associated with this party's involvement in the claim, applicable for ocean freight shipments. Identifies the specific consignment under Hague-Visby or similar maritime rules.
attributes.references: Hague-Visby Rules; FMC; IMO; MBL/HBL standards

attributes.name: contact_email
attributes.description: Primary email address of the claim contact at this party. Used for formal claim notifications, document exchange, and settlement correspondence.

attributes.name: contact_name
attributes.description: Full name of the primary contact person at this party organisation responsible for handling the claim. Used for direct correspondence and escalation.

attributes.name: contact_phone
attributes.description: Primary telephone number for the claim contact at this party. Used for urgent claim escalations and survey coordination.

attributes.name: country_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the party's registered jurisdiction. Determines applicable national regulations, customs authority jurisdiction, and governing law for the claim.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this claim party association record was first created in the Transport Shipping claims management system. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.

attributes.name: dispute_raised
attributes.description: Indicates whether this party has formally raised a dispute against the claim amount, liability determination, or settlement terms. Triggers escalation to legal proceedings or arbitration.
attributes.references: CMR Convention Article 32; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 29; ISO 9001

attributes.name: dispute_reason
attributes.description: Reason code for the dispute raised by this party. Categorises the basis of the dispute to guide resolution strategy and legal response.
attributes.references: CMR Convention; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; ISO 9001

attributes.name: document_submission_deadline
attributes.description: Deadline by which this party must submit supporting documentation (e.g., survey reports, invoices, packing lists, customs declarations) to support or defend the claim.

attributes.name: documents_received
attributes.description: Indicates whether all required supporting documents have been received from this party. Drives claim processing workflow and completeness checks.

attributes.name: iata_code
attributes.description: IATA airline or agent code assigned to this party, applicable for air carrier and freight forwarder roles. Used to identify the party in air freight claim proceedings under IATA conventions.

attributes.name: imo_number
attributes.description: IMO vessel or company identification number for ocean carrier parties. Used to identify the maritime carrier in ocean freight claims under Hague-Visby or similar rules.
attributes.references: IMO Resolution A.1078(28); Hague-Visby Rules; FMC

attributes.name: legal_representation_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether this party is represented by in-house legal counsel, external legal counsel, or has no legal representation in the claim proceedings.
attributes.references: CMR Convention; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; ISO 28000

attributes.name: liability_accepted
attributes.description: Indicates whether this party has formally accepted liability for the cargo loss, damage, or delay. Drives settlement calculation and subrogation recovery processes.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; CMR Convention; IMO Convention on Limitation of Liability

attributes.name: liability_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the liability limit amount is expressed (e.g., USD, EUR, XDR for Special Drawing Rights).
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; IMF Special Drawing Rights

attributes.name: liability_framework
attributes.description: International or contractual liability convention governing this party's exposure in the claim. Determines maximum liability limits and burden of proof requirements.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; CMR Convention; Hague-Visby Rules; COTIF Convention; IMO

attributes.name: liability_limit_amount
attributes.description: Maximum monetary liability cap applicable to this party under the governing convention or contract (e.g., SDR per kg under Warsaw-Montreal, SDR per kg under CMR). Used in settlement calculations.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 22; CMR Convention Article 23; Hague-Visby Rules Article IV

attributes.name: liability_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of total claim liability attributed to this party in cases of shared or apportioned liability across multiple carriers or intermediaries in intermodal shipments.
attributes.references: CMR Convention; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; Hague-Visby Rules

attributes.name: notification_method
attributes.description: Channel used to formally notify this party of the claim. Relevant for legal admissibility of notice under applicable conventions and SLA tracking.
attributes.references: CMR Convention Article 30; IATA Resolution 600; EDI standards

attributes.name: notification_status
attributes.description: Status of the formal claim notification sent to this party. Tracks whether the party has been formally notified per applicable convention timelines (e.g., 14-day notice under CMR, 7-day notice under Warsaw-Montreal).
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 31; CMR Convention Article 30

attributes.name: notification_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the formal claim notification was dispatched to this party. Critical for calculating statutory response deadlines under applicable liability conventions.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 31; CMR Convention Article 30

attributes.name: party_role
attributes.description: Functional role of the party within the cargo claim process. Determines liability exposure, notification obligations, and response requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: claimant|carrier|sub_carrier|insurer|underwriter|surveyor|legal_counsel|customs_authority|port_operator|freight_handler — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; CMR Convention; IMO Convention on Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims

attributes.name: party_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this party's involvement in the claim. Tracks progression from initial notification through response, dispute resolution, and final settlement or withdrawal.
attributes.references: IATA Resolution 600; CMR Convention; ISO 9001 Quality Management

attributes.name: party_type
attributes.description: Classification of the party as an organisation, individual, government body, or regulatory authority. Drives applicable liability frameworks and communication protocols.

attributes.name: power_of_attorney
attributes.description: Indicates whether a power of attorney has been received from this party authorising a representative to act on their behalf in the claim proceedings.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 6; CMR Convention; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention

attributes.name: primary_party
attributes.description: Indicates whether this party is the primary counterparty for the claim (e.g., the main claimant or the primary liable carrier) as opposed to a secondary or supporting party.

attributes.name: reference_number
attributes.description: External reference number assigned by the party to this claim (e.g., insurer claim reference, carrier incident number, surveyor job number). Enables cross-referencing with counterparty systems.

attributes.name: response_deadline
attributes.description: Contractual or statutory deadline by which this party must respond to the claim notification. Derived from notification date plus applicable convention or SLA response period.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; CMR Convention; SLA frameworks

attributes.name: response_received_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this party's formal response to the claim notification was received. Used to assess timeliness of response against statutory deadlines.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; CMR Convention Article 30

attributes.name: settlement_amount
attributes.description: Agreed monetary settlement amount attributed to or recoverable from this party. Populated upon settlement agreement and used for finance reserve accounting and credit note generation.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Finance; IFRS 37 Provisions; SOX Financial Reporting

attributes.name: settlement_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the settlement amount with this party is denominated.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; IFRS; SAP S/4HANA Finance

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: Date on which the financial settlement with this party was agreed and confirmed. Triggers finance reserve release and credit note issuance in SAP S/4HANA.

attributes.name: subrogation_applicable
attributes.description: Indicates whether subrogation rights apply to this party's involvement, enabling the insurer to pursue recovery from the liable carrier or third party after settling the claimant.
attributes.references: Insurance subrogation principles; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; CMR Convention

attributes.name: subrogation_recovery_amount
attributes.description: Amount recovered or expected to be recovered from this party through subrogation proceedings. Relevant for insurer and underwriter roles in the claim.
attributes.references: Insurance subrogation principles; IFRS 37; SAP S/4HANA Finance

attributes.name: survey_report_reference
attributes.description: Reference number of the cargo survey report issued by the surveyor party. Links the party's assessment findings to the claim record for loss quantification and liability determination.

attributes.name: surveyor_accreditation
attributes.description: Professional accreditation or certification number of the cargo surveyor party. Validates the surveyor's authority to conduct loss and damage assessments for insurance and legal purposes.

attributes.name: time_bar_date
attributes.description: Statutory limitation date by which legal action must be commenced against this party under the applicable liability convention (e.g., 2 years under Warsaw-Montreal, 1 year under CMR). Critical for claim management and legal escalation.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 35; CMR Convention Article 32; Hague-Visby Rules Article III Rule 6

attributes.name: transport_mode
attributes.description: Mode of transport under which this party's liability or involvement arises. Determines the applicable international convention (Warsaw-Montreal for air, CMR for road, Hague-Visby for ocean, COTIF for rail).
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; CMR Convention; Hague-Visby Rules; COTIF Convention

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this claim party association record was last modified. Supports audit trail, change tracking, and Silver layer incremental processing in the Databricks Lakehouse.

products.name: policy
products.description: Reference entity defining the cargo insurance policy under which a claim is filed. Captures policy number, insurer name, policy type (all-risk, named perils, war risk), coverage limit, deductible amount, policy period, covered transport modes, and special conditions. Serves as the contractual basis for claim eligibility assessment and settlement calculation. Distinct from the contract domain which manages carrier and customer service contracts.

attributes.name: policy_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the cargo insurance policy record within the Transport Shipping data platform. Primary key for the claim_policy entity.

attributes.name: aggregate_annual_limit_amount
attributes.description: Maximum total insurer liability across all claims filed within the policy year, expressed in coverage_limit_currency. Once exhausted, no further claims are payable under this policy until renewal. Critical for reserve accounting in SAP S/4HANA Finance.
attributes.references: IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts; SOX Section 404; Institute Cargo Clauses

attributes.name: auto_renewal_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this policy automatically renews at expiry without requiring explicit action from Transport Shipping. When True, cancellation notice must be given before the renewal_date to prevent automatic continuation.
attributes.references: IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts; Institute Cargo Clauses

attributes.name: broker_name
attributes.description: Name of the insurance broker or intermediary who placed this policy on behalf of Transport Shipping. The broker is the primary point of contact for policy renewals, endorsements, and claim escalations.
attributes.references: IATA Cargo Insurance Guidelines; FMC Regulations

attributes.name: broker_reference
attributes.description: Broker's own reference number for this policy placement. Used in broker correspondence, premium invoices, and claim notifications routed through the broker.

attributes.name: cancellation_notice_period_days
attributes.description: Minimum number of calendar days' written notice required by either party to cancel this policy before its expiry_date. Breach of this period may result in premium liability for the full policy term.
attributes.references: Institute Cargo Clauses — Lloyd's Market Association; IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts

attributes.name: cargo_category
attributes.description: Classification of cargo types covered under this policy. Determines applicable liability frameworks and special conditions. 'dangerous_goods' aligns to IMDG Code and ICAO Technical Instructions; 'high_value' triggers enhanced survey requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: general|perishable|dangerous_goods|high_value|fragile|bulk|pharmaceutical|automotive — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IMDG Code (IMO); ICAO Technical Instructions for Dangerous Goods; IATA DGR

attributes.name: claims_filing_period_days
attributes.description: Maximum number of calendar days after the loss event within which a formal claim must be filed with the insurer. Distinct from the notification period; this is the hard deadline for submitting full claim documentation.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 35; CMR Convention Article 32; IMO Hague-Visby Rules Article III Rule 6

attributes.name: claims_notification_period_days
attributes.description: Maximum number of calendar days after discovery of loss or damage within which a claim must be notified to the insurer to remain eligible for settlement. Breach of this period may void the claim. Aligned to IATA, CMR, and IMO convention time limits.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 31; CMR Convention Article 30; IMO Hague-Visby Rules Article III Rule 6

attributes.name: co_insurance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this policy is co-insured by multiple underwriters sharing the risk proportionally. When True, the co_insurance_lead_insurer and individual underwriter shares must be tracked for claim apportionment.
attributes.references: Lloyd's Market Association Co-Insurance Clauses; IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts

attributes.name: co_insurance_share_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of the total risk retained by the lead insurer named in insurer_name when this is a co-insured policy. Expressed as a decimal percentage (e.g., 60.00 for 60%). Only applicable when co_insurance_flag is True.
attributes.references: Lloyd's Market Association Co-Insurance Clauses; IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts

attributes.name: coverage_limit_amount
attributes.description: Maximum monetary amount the insurer will pay for any single claim or in aggregate under this policy, expressed in the policy currency. Serves as the upper bound for settlement calculations. Critical for claim eligibility assessment.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; CMR Convention Article 23; IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts

attributes.name: coverage_limit_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the coverage limit amount and deductible are denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Required for multi-currency settlement calculations.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts

attributes.name: covered_transport_modes
attributes.description: Pipe-delimited list of transport modes covered under this policy (e.g., 'air|ocean|road|rail'). Determines claim eligibility based on the mode used for the shipment. Aligned to IATA (air), IMO (ocean), CMR Convention (road), and CIM/COTIF (rail) liability frameworks. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: air|ocean|road|rail|multimodal|courier — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; IMO Hague-Visby Rules; CMR Convention; CIM/COTIF Rail Convention

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this claim policy record was first created in the Transport Shipping data platform. Populated automatically at insert time. Used for data lineage, audit trails, and SOX compliance. Maps to RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED canonical category.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; GDPR Article 5(2) Accountability; ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems

attributes.name: dangerous_goods_covered
attributes.description: Indicates whether this policy explicitly covers dangerous goods shipments as classified under the IMDG Code (ocean), ICAO Technical Instructions (air), or ADR/RID (road/rail). When True, the policy must reference applicable DG endorsements and special conditions.
attributes.references: IMDG Code (IMO); ICAO Technical Instructions for Dangerous Goods; ADR/RID Regulations

attributes.name: declaration_period_days
attributes.description: Number of calendar days after shipment dispatch within which a declaration must be submitted to the insurer under an open cover policy. Only applicable when declaration_required_flag is True. Null for specific voyage policies.
attributes.references: Institute Cargo Clauses — Lloyd's Market Association

attributes.name: declaration_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether individual shipment declarations must be submitted to the insurer under this open cover policy. When True, each shipment must be declared within the agreed declaration period to activate coverage for that consignment.
attributes.references: Institute Cargo Clauses — Lloyd's Market Association; IATA Cargo Insurance Guidelines

attributes.name: deductible_amount
attributes.description: Fixed monetary amount that Transport Shipping must absorb before the insurer's liability commences on any individual claim. Deducted from gross claim settlement to arrive at net insurer payment. Expressed in coverage_limit_currency.
attributes.references: Institute Cargo Clauses — Lloyd's Market Association; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention

attributes.name: deductible_type
attributes.description: Method by which the deductible is applied. 'fixed' is a flat monetary amount; 'percentage' is a proportion of the claim value; 'franchise' means the deductible is waived if the claim exceeds the threshold; 'nil' means no deductible applies.
attributes.references: Institute Cargo Clauses — Lloyd's Market Association

attributes.name: dispute_resolution_method
attributes.description: Agreed mechanism for resolving disputes between Transport Shipping and the insurer regarding claim settlements or policy interpretation. 'arbitration' is most common in international cargo insurance under Lloyd's and London Market policies.
attributes.references: IMO FAL Convention; IATA Resolution 600a; ICC Arbitration Rules

attributes.name: document_reference
attributes.description: Document management system reference or URL pointing to the signed policy wording, schedule, and endorsements stored in the enterprise content management system. Enables auditors and claims handlers to retrieve the authoritative policy text.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404 Document Retention; ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the cargo insurance policy becomes binding and coverage commences. Used to determine claim eligibility based on shipment date. Maps to EFFECTIVE_FROM canonical category for MASTER_AGREEMENT role.
attributes.references: Institute Cargo Clauses — Lloyd's Market Association; IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts

attributes.name: exclusions
attributes.description: Structured description of risks, cargo types, or circumstances explicitly excluded from coverage under this policy. Common exclusions include inherent vice, delay, inadequate packing, and nuclear risks. Used during claim eligibility assessment.
attributes.references: Institute Cargo Clauses (A, B, C) — Lloyd's Market Association; IMDG Code (IMO)

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the cargo insurance policy coverage terminates. Claims for shipments dispatched after this date are not eligible under this policy. Nullable for open-ended or evergreen open cover policies. Maps to EFFECTIVE_UNTIL canonical category for MASTER_AGREEMENT role.
attributes.references: Institute Cargo Clauses — Lloyd's Market Association; IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts

attributes.name: geographic_scope
attributes.description: Territorial extent of coverage under this policy. 'worldwide' covers all global shipments; 'regional' covers a defined geographic region; 'domestic' covers in-country shipments only; 'cross_border' covers international shipments excluding domestic legs.
attributes.references: WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement; IMO FAL Convention; WCO Framework of Standards

attributes.name: governing_law
attributes.description: Jurisdiction whose laws govern the interpretation and enforcement of this insurance policy (e.g., 'English Law', 'New York Law', 'German Law'). Determines dispute resolution forum and applicable legal standards for claim settlement.
attributes.references: IMO FAL Convention; WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement; IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts

attributes.name: insurer_name
attributes.description: Legal trading name of the insurance company or underwriting syndicate that issued the cargo insurance policy. Used in insurer correspondence, claim submissions, and settlement negotiations.

attributes.name: insurer_policy_reference
attributes.description: Insurer's own internal reference or certificate number for this policy, distinct from the policy_number used by Transport Shipping. Required for direct insurer correspondence and electronic claim submission via EDI.
attributes.references: IATA e-freight EDI Standards; IMO FAL Convention

attributes.name: issuing_country
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the jurisdiction in which this insurance policy was issued. Determines applicable regulatory oversight (e.g., FCA in GBR, BaFin in DEU, NAIC in USA) and tax treatment of premiums.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; GDPR Article 3; IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts

attributes.name: liability_basis
attributes.description: Valuation method used to calculate the insured value of cargo for settlement purposes. 'invoice_value' uses the commercial invoice amount; 'declared_value' uses the shipper-declared value on the AWB or BOL; 'market_value' uses prevailing market price at destination; 'replacement_cost' uses the cost to replace the goods.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; CMR Convention; IMO Hague-Visby Rules; Institute Cargo Clauses

attributes.name: open_cover_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this policy is structured as an open cover (blanket policy covering all qualifying shipments automatically without individual declaration) rather than a specific voyage or shipment policy. Open cover policies are common for high-volume freight forwarders.
attributes.references: Institute Cargo Clauses — Lloyd's Market Association; IATA Cargo Insurance Guidelines

attributes.name: per_shipment_limit_amount
attributes.description: Maximum insurer liability for any single shipment event under this policy, expressed in coverage_limit_currency. May be lower than the aggregate coverage_limit_amount. Used in claim settlement calculations for individual AWB, BOL, or consignment note events.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 22; CMR Convention Article 23; IMO Hague-Visby Rules

attributes.name: policy_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric identifier assigned by the insurer to uniquely identify the cargo insurance policy. Used in all insurer correspondence, claim filings, and settlement documentation. Maps to the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER canonical category for MASTER_AGREEMENT role.

attributes.name: policy_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the cargo insurance policy. 'active' indicates the policy is in force and eligible for claim filing; 'suspended' indicates temporary coverage halt; 'expired' indicates the policy period has ended without renewal; 'cancelled' indicates early termination; 'pending_renewal' indicates renewal is in progress; 'lapsed' indicates non-renewal after expiry. Maps to LIFECYCLE_STATUS canonical category.
attributes.references: ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems; IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts

attributes.name: policy_type
attributes.description: Classification of the cargo insurance policy by coverage scope. 'all_risk' covers all physical loss or damage except named exclusions; 'named_perils' covers only explicitly listed risks; 'war_risk' covers war, strikes, and political risks; 'total_loss_only' covers only complete cargo loss; 'open_cover' is a continuous blanket policy for multiple shipments. Maps to CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE canonical category.
attributes.references: Institute Cargo Clauses (A, B, C) — Lloyd's Market Association; IATA Cargo Insurance Guidelines

attributes.name: premium_amount
attributes.description: Annual or periodic insurance premium paid by Transport Shipping to the insurer for this policy. Used in finance for cost allocation, OPEX reporting, and profitability analysis per trade lane or business unit.
attributes.references: IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts; SOX Section 404 Financial Reporting

attributes.name: premium_payment_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which the insurance premium is paid to the insurer. Drives accounts payable scheduling in SAP S/4HANA Finance and cash flow forecasting.
attributes.references: IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts; SAP S/4HANA Finance AP Module

attributes.name: reinsurance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the insurer has placed reinsurance for this policy. Relevant for large-value cargo policies where the insurer's net retention is limited. Affects claim recovery timelines and insurer solvency risk assessment.
attributes.references: IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts; Lloyd's Market Association Reinsurance Clauses

attributes.name: renewal_date
attributes.description: Date on which the policy is due for renewal. Used to trigger renewal negotiations, premium reviews, and coverage reassessment. Typically aligns with or precedes the expiry_date.
attributes.references: IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts; ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems

attributes.name: special_conditions
attributes.description: Free-text field capturing policy-specific endorsements, exclusions, warranties, or special clauses that modify the standard Institute Cargo Clauses terms. Examples include temperature warranty for perishables, packing warranty, or exclusion of specific trade lanes.
attributes.references: Institute Cargo Clauses — Lloyd's Market Association; IATA Cargo Insurance Guidelines

attributes.name: subrogation_rights
attributes.description: Indicates whether the insurer retains the right of subrogation to pursue recovery from liable third parties (carriers, handlers, customs authorities) after settling a claim. When True, Transport Shipping must cooperate with insurer recovery actions and preserve evidence.
attributes.references: CMR Convention Article 37; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 37; IMO Hague-Visby Rules

attributes.name: survey_required_threshold_amount
attributes.description: Minimum claim value (in coverage_limit_currency) above which an independent cargo survey report is mandatory before the insurer will process the claim. Below this threshold, claims may be settled on documentary evidence alone.
attributes.references: Institute Cargo Clauses — Lloyd's Market Association; IATA Cargo Claims Handling Manual

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this claim policy record was last modified in the Transport Shipping data platform. Updated on every write operation. Used for change data capture, incremental ETL processing, and audit compliance.
attributes.references: SOX Section 404; GDPR Article 5(2) Accountability; ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems

products.name: recovery_action
products.description: Transactional record tracking individual recovery actions taken against liable third parties (sub-carriers, port operators, freight handlers) as part of subrogation or direct carrier recovery. Captures action type (demand letter, legal filing, arbitration, settlement negotiation), action date, responsible party, amount demanded, amount recovered, and action outcome. Supports the full subrogation workflow and recovery P&L tracking.

attributes.name: recovery_action_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for each recovery action record within the subrogation or direct carrier recovery workflow.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to contract.agreement. Business justification: Demand letters and legal filings reference contractual liability provisions, limitation periods, and dispute resolution clauses. Essential for recovery strategy, determining jurisdiction, and establis

attributes.name: bill_of_lading_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to freight.bill_of_lading. Business justification: Ocean cargo recovery requires B/L reference to identify liable carrier and enforce liability limits. Replaces denormalized bol_number with proper FK for carrier identification, Hague-Visby rules enfor

attributes.name: booking_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to freight.booking. Business justification: Recovery actions may reference booking for pre-shipment contractual breaches (space confirmation failure, rate dispute). Supports booking-level recovery demand and pre-shipment contractual breach enfo

attributes.description: Reference to the parent cargo insurance claim against which this recovery action is being pursued. Links the recovery action to the originating loss or damage event.

attributes.name: cargo_survey_id

attributes.name: carrier_id

attributes.name: chart_of_accounts_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.chart_of_accounts. Business justification: Recovery transactions require GL account assignment for expense and income classification, enabling proper P&L presentation and tracking of net recovery effectiveness.

attributes.name: claim_party_id
attributes.description: Reference to the third-party entity (sub-carrier, port operator, freight handler, warehouse operator) held liable and against whom the recovery action is directed. Primary counterparty reference for this transaction.
attributes.references: CMR Convention; IMO Convention; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; FMC Regulations

attributes.name: company_code_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.company_code. Business justification: Recovery actions generate financial transactions (legal costs, settlements, recoveries) that must be posted to a legal entity for financial statement preparation and intercompany reconciliation.

attributes.name: consignment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the internal shipment record associated with the cargo loss or damage event underlying this recovery action. Links to SAP TM or Oracle TMS shipment execution records.

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Legal costs and recovery expenses must be allocated to cost centers for budget control, variance analysis, and tracking of recovery program costs against recovered amounts.

attributes.name: customer_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.customer_account. Business justification: Recovery actions may involve customer accounts when customer liability is determined (e.g., shipper negligence). Enables customer-level recovery tracking, customer liability reporting, and customer co

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the internal employee or team responsible for managing and progressing this recovery action. Used for workload assignment, escalation, and performance tracking in Workday HCM.

attributes.name: facility_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to warehouse.facility. Business justification: Recovery actions require facility attribution for cost center allocation, GL account coding, and tracking facility-specific recovery rates. Critical for financial reporting, facility P&L statements, a

attributes.name: freight_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to freight.freight_order. Business justification: Recovery actions pursue reimbursement from liable parties for specific freight orders. Essential for identifying liable carrier from freight order, calculating recovery amount based on freight charges

attributes.name: hse_incident_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.hse_incident. Business justification: Recovery actions may target parties responsible for HSE incidents that caused cargo loss (facility operator negligence, carrier safety violations). Legal teams require HSE incident documentation for d

attributes.name: lane_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to route.lane. Business justification: Recovery demands reference lane-specific carrier agreements to establish liability basis, statutory limits, and contractual remedies. Enables tracking of recovery success rates by lane and carrier for

attributes.name: subrogation_case_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to claim.subrogation_case. Business justification: Recovery actions are tactical steps taken within a strategic subrogation case. N:1 relationship (many recovery actions per subrogation case). A subrogation case may involve multiple recovery actions (

attributes.name: supplier_id
attributes.description: Reference to the cargo insurer involved in the subrogation process. Identifies the insurer to whom the insurer share of recovery proceeds must be remitted.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Finance; ISO 28000; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention

attributes.name: transport_document_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to document.transport_document. Business justification: Legal filings (court complaints, arbitration notices) are specific document instances required for litigation management. Legal teams track legal_filing_date and court_case_number but need the actual

attributes.name: action_date
attributes.description: The real-world business date on which the recovery action was formally initiated or executed (e.g., date a demand letter was issued, date a legal filing was lodged). Distinct from the record creation timestamp.
attributes.references: CMR Convention; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; IMO Hague-Visby Rules

attributes.name: action_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field capturing key correspondence summaries, negotiation positions, legal strategy notes, and material developments in the recovery action. Supports case management and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: ISO 9001 Quality Management; SOX Compliance; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: action_outcome
attributes.description: Final result of the recovery action upon closure. Indicates whether the full demanded amount, a partial amount, or nothing was recovered. Drives reserve release and P&L recognition in SAP S/4HANA Finance.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Finance; IFRS 9; ISO 9001 Quality Management

attributes.name: action_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference number assigned to this recovery action, used in correspondence with liable third parties, legal counsel, and insurers. Follows the format RA-YYYY-NNNNNN.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Finance AR Module; ISO 28000

attributes.name: action_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the recovery action, tracking progression from initiation through resolution. Drives workflow routing and P&L reserve adjustments in SAP S/4HANA Finance.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Finance; ISO 9001 Quality Management

attributes.name: action_type
attributes.description: Classification of the recovery action being taken against the liable third party. Indicates the legal or commercial mechanism employed. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: demand_letter|legal_filing|arbitration|settlement_negotiation|mediation|subrogation_notice — promote to reference product if additional types are required]
attributes.references: CMR Convention; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; IMO Convention; FMC Regulations

attributes.name: arbitration_body
attributes.description: Name of the arbitration institution or tribunal handling the dispute where action type is arbitration (e.g., ICC International Court of Arbitration, LMAA, AAA). Null for non-arbitration action types.
attributes.references: UNCITRAL Arbitration Rules; ICC Arbitration Rules; LMAA Terms; FMC Regulations

attributes.name: court_case_number
attributes.description: Official case reference number assigned by the court or tribunal where a legal filing has been lodged. Applicable only when action type is legal_filing. Used for docket tracking and legal correspondence.
attributes.references: US DOT; FMC Regulations; CMR Convention; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp recording when this recovery action record was first created in the data platform. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and SOX compliance reporting.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance; GDPR Article 5; ISO 9001; SAP S/4HANA Finance

attributes.name: dangerous_goods_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the cargo involved in the underlying loss event was classified as dangerous goods. Triggers additional regulatory reporting requirements under IMDG Code or ICAO Technical Instructions and may affect liability limits.
attributes.references: IMDG Code; ICAO Technical Instructions for Dangerous Goods; IMO Convention; IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations

attributes.name: demanded_amount
attributes.description: Gross monetary amount formally demanded from the liable third party in this recovery action, expressed in the transaction currency. Represents the full claim value before any negotiated reduction or statutory cap.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Finance AR Module; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; CMR Convention; IFRS 9

attributes.name: escalation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this recovery action has been escalated to senior management, legal leadership, or external counsel due to complexity, high value, or imminent limitation period expiry.
attributes.references: ISO 9001 Quality Management; SAP S/4HANA Finance

attributes.name: external_counsel_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or name of the external legal counsel or law firm engaged to pursue this recovery action. Used for legal spend tracking and matter management.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Finance; Coupa Procurement; SOX Compliance

attributes.name: insurer_notification_date
attributes.description: Date on which the insurer was formally notified of the recovery action being pursued on their behalf under subrogation rights. Required for insurer correspondence audit trail.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; CMR Convention; ISO 28000; GDPR Article 33

attributes.name: insurer_share_amount
attributes.description: Portion of the recovered amount attributable to the insurer under subrogation rights. Represents the amount to be remitted to the insurer from the total recovery proceeds.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Finance AR Module; IFRS 9; Insurance Subrogation Principles

attributes.name: jurisdiction_country
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the legal jurisdiction in which the recovery action is being pursued. Determines applicable procedural law, court system, and enforcement mechanisms.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1; CMR Convention; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; WTO; UNCITRAL

attributes.name: legal_costs
attributes.description: Total legal and professional fees incurred in pursuing this recovery action (attorney fees, court filing fees, arbitration fees). Deducted from gross recovery to calculate net recovery P&L.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Finance OPEX Accounting; IFRS 9; SOX Compliance

attributes.name: liability_convention
attributes.description: International liability convention governing the maximum recoverable amount and burden of proof for this recovery action. Determines statutory limits applied to the demanded amount.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; CMR Convention; IMO Hague-Visby Rules; COTIF-CIM Convention; UNCITRAL

attributes.name: liable_party_name
attributes.description: Legal or trading name of the third-party entity against whom the recovery action is directed (e.g., sub-carrier, port terminal operator, freight handler). Captured for correspondence and legal documentation purposes.
attributes.references: CMR Convention; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; GDPR Article 4

attributes.name: liable_party_type
attributes.description: Classification of the liable third party by their operational role in the logistics chain. Determines applicable liability convention and recovery limits. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: sub_carrier|port_operator|freight_handler|warehouse_operator|customs_broker|nvocc — promote to reference product if additional types are required]
attributes.references: CMR Convention; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; IMO Convention; FMC Regulations

attributes.name: limitation_period_expiry_date
attributes.description: Statutory deadline by which the recovery action must be formally filed or concluded under the applicable liability convention (e.g., 2 years under Warsaw-Montreal, 1 year under CMR). Critical for legal compliance and action prioritization.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 35; CMR Convention Article 32; IMO Hague-Visby Rules Article III Rule 6

attributes.name: loss_type
attributes.description: Nature of the cargo loss or damage event that gave rise to the recovery action. Determines applicable liability provisions and evidentiary requirements under the governing convention.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; CMR Convention; IMO Hague-Visby Rules; IMDG Code

attributes.name: net_recovery_amount
attributes.description: Net monetary benefit realized from the recovery action after deducting legal costs and any insurer share from the gross recovered amount. Primary P&L metric for recovery performance reporting.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Finance; IFRS 9; SOX; EBITDA Reporting

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Business priority assigned to this recovery action based on demanded amount, limitation period proximity, and strategic importance. Drives case handler workload prioritization and escalation thresholds.
attributes.references: ISO 9001 Quality Management; SAP S/4HANA Finance

attributes.name: recovered_amount
attributes.description: Actual monetary amount successfully recovered from the liable third party upon conclusion of the recovery action. May be less than the demanded amount due to negotiation, statutory caps, or partial liability acceptance.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Finance AR Module; IFRS 9; ISO 9001

attributes.name: recovery_basis
attributes.description: Legal or contractual basis under which the recovery action is pursued. Subrogation arises when the insurer recovers from the liable party after paying the insured; direct carrier recovery is pursued by the shipper or 3PL directly.
attributes.references: CMR Convention; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; IMO Hague-Visby Rules; ISO 28000

attributes.name: recovery_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the demanded and recovered amounts are denominated (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Required for multi-currency P&L reporting and FX conversion in SAP S/4HANA Finance.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; IFRS 9; SAP S/4HANA Finance

attributes.name: reserve_amount
attributes.description: Financial reserve set aside in the general ledger for the expected recovery proceeds from this action. Managed in SAP S/4HANA Finance for IFRS 9 expected credit loss provisioning and P&L reserve accounting.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Finance GL Module; IFRS 9; SOX Compliance; IFRS 37 Provisions

attributes.name: resolution_date
attributes.description: Date on which the recovery action was formally concluded, whether through settlement, withdrawal, legal judgment, or arbitration award. Null if action is still open.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Finance; CMR Convention; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention

attributes.name: response_due_date
attributes.description: Contractual or statutory deadline by which the liable third party must respond to the recovery action. Used for SLA monitoring and escalation triggering.
attributes.references: CMR Convention Article 32; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 35; ISO 9001

attributes.name: settlement_agreement_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier of the executed settlement agreement where the recovery action was resolved through negotiated settlement. Links to the contract management system for document retrieval.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA Finance; ISO 9001; CMR Convention; IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention

attributes.name: statutory_liability_limit
attributes.description: Maximum recoverable amount permitted under the applicable international liability convention (e.g., SDR per kg under Warsaw-Montreal, SDR per kg under CMR). Used to cap the demanded amount where applicable.
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention Article 22; CMR Convention Article 23; IMO Hague-Visby Rules Article IV

attributes.name: transport_mode
attributes.description: Mode of transport applicable to the underlying shipment loss or damage event, determining the governing liability convention (e.g., IATA Warsaw-Montreal for air, CMR for road, Hague-Visby for ocean).
attributes.references: IATA Warsaw-Montreal Convention; CMR Convention; IMO Hague-Visby Rules; ICAO Technical Instructions

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp recording the most recent modification to this recovery action record. Supports change data capture, audit trail, and data quality monitoring in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: SOX Compliance; GDPR Article 5; ISO 9001; Databricks Lakehouse
